articleTitle: A digital correlator for real time spectral analysis of radio astronomy signals
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper describes the arithmetic section of a digital correlator, which is used in conjunction with a mini-computer to perform real time spectral analysis of radio astronomy spectral line signals, having bandwidths of up to 5, 12 MHz. The radio astronomy signals are both noiselike and deeply buried in noise, much of which is contributed by the receiving system. The correlator employs 1 024 identical ‘channels’ to calculate correlation coefficients for 1 024 different values of delay. Each channel is capable of performing a multiplication and addition every 97,6 ns. The input signal is coarsely quantized into three levels (–1, 0 or + 1) in order to simplify the correlator circuitry at the expense of signal to noise ratio. By varying the clock rate, spectral bandwidths from 40 kHz to 5, 12 MHz may be analysed. The instrument may be used as a single 1 024 channel, dual 512 channel or quad 256 channel correlator. Both auto-correlation and cross-correlation may be performed on up to four signals or pairs of signals. After Fourier transformation of the correlation function, in the mini-computer, a power spectrum or cross-power spectrum is obtained, At present 256 channels are in operation. Results of observation of the formaldehyde absorption spectral line are presented.

articleTitle: Omgewingsbestuur — nuwe tegnologie of nuwe filosofie?
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: After the historical development of engineering has been outlined to arrive at the concept of ‘environmental design’, the chaos currently present in some countries is discussed briefly in order to define its multiple cause. Subsequently the multiple solution to the problem is indicated, stressing that it has mainly a philosophical character, without which the process of environmental impact control, which is also discussed in general, cannot be executed effectively. It is explained that the appropriate philosophy centres around the proper definition of ‘environment’, and that the issue at stake is really the maintenance of balance between nature conservation and cultural development. Finally, the matrix and mapping techniques for documenting data in the environmental impact analysis process are discussed briefly.

abstract: The pattern of education of almost all Professional Engineers by means of four-year Bachelor's degrees and subsequent training in industry is well established in this country. The degree course aims to provide the graduate with the basic scientific and engineering knowledge together with a necessarily limited amount of instruction in more specialised areas. The latter aspect becomes more difficult to handle as the amount of overall knowledge and technology increases and new specialities grow. A degree course in electrical engineering can only hope to provide a finite amount of specialised study in the later years with the objective of teaching the student how to cope with a new field and build on his existing knowledge. It is clearly understood by many engineers and employers that continued intellectual, technical and managerial development after graduation is the key to a satisfactory career.

abstract: A short overview of the development of digital signal processing is presented. This is limited to classical areas of processing in the time or frequency domain using Fourier transformations, spectral analysis, filtering, correlation of convulation. Prior to the introduction of the Fast Fourier Transform (FFT), digital signal processing in engineering applications was limited mainly to time domain solutions. The FFT opened up the whole field of frequency domain processing for digital techniques. This in turn stimulated the development of new algorithms or methods for solving of problems which in the put were not possible with analogue techniques. After a brief review of early developments and means for information reduction, the FFT, the chirp Z-transform, the Cepstrum, Fast Number Transform, linear prediction and adaptive filtering, are discussed.

articleTitle: The characteristics and application of vacuum switching devices
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Vacuum switching devices arc enjoying rapidly increasing popularity in medium voltage applications. They have many attractive features resulting from the unique are extinction process in vacuum and these have spurred development in this direction. However, in early application the full implications of their exceptional rate of dielectric recovery were not appreciated and in some cases insulation damage has been caused in low impulse strength and high surge impedence load circuits. Much work has since been done to investigate transient voltages associated with vacuum switching devices, and it can confidently be said that these are now well understood. By judicious use of suppressor equipment when necessary, the advantages of these devices can be enjoyed without fear of damage to the insulation system of the switched equipment.

abstract: The paper deals with improvements on the EMI susceptibility of computer systems. The initial step in solving EMC problems is always the assessment of the electromagnetic environment. The instruments and diagnostic methods are described in detail. The next Step it usually the inspection of the grounding system, with measurements, and the search for and elimination of ground loops. Logic ground, mains ground and virtual ground systems are discussed. Finally Improvements of the quality of the mains supply, which involves the motor alternators, isolation transformers, constant voltage transformers, varistors and transzorb devices, are considered.

abstract: Dr Ralph Blyth Anderson was born in 1916 in Bulawayo and educated at the Milton High School there. In 1937, he was awarded the degree of BSc (Engineering) at Cape Town. He worked with the Southern Rhodesia Electricity Supply Commission and, together with Mr R D Jenner, was awarded the Gold Medal of the Institute for a paper on Lightning published in the Transactions in 1954. In 1965 he joined the CSIR and is now Head of the Power Electrical Engineering Division of the National Electrical Engineering Research Institute. He was appointed Convenor of the Working Group 33.01 (Lightning) of Study Committee No. 33 of CIGRE (International Conference on Large Electric Systems at High Tension) as from January 1970 after service with the Working Group since 1963. He was awarded the degree of Doctor of Philosophy by the University of Cape Town in December, 1972 for a thesis entitled ‘The Lightning Discharge.‘ Dr Anderson is the author of a number of papers, many jointly with colleagues.

articleTitle: Lightning overvoltages in a rural distribution line — preliminary results
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Preliminary data are presented from measurements carried out on a 10 km length of 11 kV test line during the 1978/79 thunderstorm season in respect of direct strokes to the line and Induced overvoltage surge characteristics. The majority of lightning surges are caused by induction from nearby discharges to ground, are of positive polarity, rarely exceed 100 kV, and are accountable in term of classic electromagnetic field theories. Several bipolar surge records have also been obtained however, whose characteristics deviate considerably from theoretical prediction, and it Is considered that this might be due to the influence of the leader mechanism.

articleTitle: Applications of total modulation which aid the analysis of ac motors and their solid state drives
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: There are severe limitations to the connection end location of the coils of a tutor winding so that they produce a satisfactory revolving field. The influence of these restrictions can be formulated in terms of modulating functions which yield a series of revolving field components. This technique is readily extended co solid state frequency and voltage converters in which the stator phase connections are continuously altered relative to the supply. Relationships are preserved which enable the calculation of the angular velocities and magnitudes of the revolving fields produced by a practical stator winding when excited by a fundamental and a series of harmonic voltages. Converter output voltages may be calculated and it is shown how motor currents may then be reconverted to find the supply currents.

articleTitle: An ‘equivalent circuit’ approach to interference analysis
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: In this paper an attempt is made to explain a wide variety of observed Interference phenomena by means of a theoretical model. A system is analysed in terms of an interference source circuit, an interference receiving circuit and the possible couplings which can exist between the two. Simple equivalent circuits are proposed and the transfer of interference from source to receiver is analysed by means of frequency transfer function techniques. It is shown that earth structures play a very important role in these situations and the role of earth connections, screens etc in suppressing interference is analysed.

articleTitle: Electrical interference and protection of telemetry systems in an underground mine
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The majority of telemetry systems installed in (old mines rely on at least a pair of wires as the transmission medium. The wires are generally part of a mullicara armoured cable which often there the same cable duct at 6,6 kV, 520 V and 110 V power cables. Other cables in the vicinity may carry telephone or control signals. The stray coupling of electric currents between these cables, and in particular between pairs in the tame cable, results in interference with a telemetry signal. This paper indicates the likely interference sources and the magnitude and frequency spectra of the induced noise measured on various types of underground cables.

articleTitle: A feasibility study of the realization of adaptive equalizers with microprocessors
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: In spread spectrum data transmission systems employing pseudo-random type signals and microprocessor realizations. FFT techniques are indicated for computational economy. This offers the possibility of combining the functions of channel equalization and character recognition. This study concentrated on the aspect of channel equalization as representative of most of the functions required in a fully fledged system. The results indicate that (I) even if only equalization is considered, the use of a bit slice processor supported by a fast hardware multiplier is imperative; (2) such a processor could alternatively provide a weighted DFT output instead of a filtered time sequence to that the subsequent processor may affect character recognition without reprocessing the filtered time sequence and (3) for the particular processor considered time domain filtering is about twice as fast as frequency domain filtering.

abstract: This paper attempts to explain the Discrete Fourier Transform in terms of its action on real pulse and sinusoidal data. Even real data is seen to give rise to even real spectra, and odd real data produces odd imaginary spectra. The idea of aliases, leakage and windows are examined. The Fast Fourier Transform is a method of performing the DFT and it is approached firstly by decimation in time and then by decimation in frequency. The terms twiddle factor, bit reversal, shuffling, butterflies and radix are Introduced. Application of the FFT in correlation, convolution, band limited interpolation and coherence functions is discussed. The Chirp Z Transform performed by convolution in a transversal filter is examined, as it seems to be the cheapest and fastest method of performing the DFT.

publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: An introductory courte on linear discrete time systems can conveniently be offered before or together with one on continuous time systems, and furthermore it is desirable that such a course should be presented as early as possible in the syllabus. Such a course could start with a description of a linear discrete time system in terms of difference equations, followed by a discussion of the Z-transform without the students having to know anything about the Fourier Transform. Stress should be laid on the connection between difference equations, transfer functions, pole-zero diagrams, frequency responses, impulse responses and convolution.

abstract: The piper outlines the basic mechanisms of switching surge generation when switching inductive toads, and emphasises the importance of a full understanding of the transient interactions amongst the relevant system parameters. The need for wave-shaping principles of surge suppression, rather than overvoltage limitation, it demonstrated with particular emphasis upon the advantages of resistively damped surge capacitors. A co-ordinated approach illustrating a method for arriving at optimised solutions to surge suppression problems is also briefly described.

abstract: Was born in 1926, was brought up on the Consolidated Main Reef and City Deep Gold Mines, was educated at Marist Brothers College, Observatory, Johannesburg, served in the SA Corps of Signals, graduated from Witwatersrand University in 1949 and has worked for the SABC since the beginning of 1950, when he started as a workshop mechanician. He is at present the Director of Technical Services of that same organisation. He has four children, two boys and two girls between the ages of 17 and 23. He was a widower until fortune smiled on him in the form of Dr Frances Lewer-Allen. He has represented the SABC and been a South African delegate at various International Conferences. He has read papers at International Conventions in Hamburg, Brussels, Montreux, London and Sydney, and has chaired sessions at the International Broadcasting Convention in London several times. On behalf of this Institute and the Engineering Profession he is involved with SACPE on Council, the Professional Advisory Committee on Electrical Engineering and the Registration Committee. He is a member of FSPE's Executive Committee and an additional member of FSPE's Board. He is also a Past Chairman of the Light Current Section of this Institute and has been a member of the Institute since 1948 and a Council Member since 1969. He says that he is a mediocre shot with pistol, rifle and shot gun and has his time cut out competing with Frances who is a good rifle shot. He sails whenever he can, tries to play tennis and has woodwork and trying to keep out of debt as additional hobbies.

articleTitle: Suppression of longitudinal interference from railway and other sources into higher grade open wire telephone routes
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: With the high voltage 50 Hz electrification of certain main RSA Railway routes came the problem of induction of this low frequency and its harmonics into open wire carrier lines which run parallel to the railways. Because of the accurately balanced exposure and the immaculate construction of these open wire lines the effect of induction is primarily in the longitudinal or common mode sense. High Induced voltages, besides being personnel hazards, eventually results in degraded performance so it is necessary to break up each pair of wires into sections to limit this effect.
